chunks: And through this chain of narration from Hibatullah ibn Muhammad, son of the daughter of Umm Kulthum, daughter of Abu Ja'far al-Amari, who said: Umm Kulthum, daughter of Abu Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him) told me, saying: Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) was the representative of Abu Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him) for many years, overseeing his properties and delivering his secrets to the chiefs of the Shia. He was his intimate associate, to the extent that he would tell him about what occurred between him and his concubines due to his proximity and affinity. She said: He would give him thirty dinars every month as a stipend, in addition to what he received from the ministers and chiefs of the Shia, such as Aal al-Furat and others, due to his prestige, position, and high status among them. This created a profound impression in the hearts of the Shia regarding his special connection to my father, their endorsement of his trustworthiness, and the dissemination of his excellence, piety, and the qualities he bore from this matter. Thus, affairs were facilitated for him during the lifetime of my father until the final will explicitly designated him for that position. No one disputed his authority or doubted it, except one who was ignorant of my father's affairs first, and I do not know of anyone from the Shia who questioned it. I have heard this from more than one member of the Banu Nuwaybah, such as Abu al-Hasan ibn Kibriya and others.

key_terms.آلُ الْفُرَاتِ: Aal al-Furat, a prominent family of Shia chiefs and ministers
key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ رُوحٍ: Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a key figure in the Minor Occultation
key_terms.بَنُو نُوْبَخْتٍ: Banu Nuwaybah, a notable family of Shia scholars and officials

ai.seo_question: Who was Husayn ibn Ruh and what was his role as the Imam's representative?
ai.summary: This narration from Umm Kulthum, daughter of Imam al-Hadi, underscores the high status of Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh as the 'Special Emissary' (al-Wakil al-Khas) during the Minor Occultation, highlighting his unique intimacy with the Imam and his substantial financial stipend from the Shia community. It emphasizes that his authority was undisputed and well-known among the elite, serving as a crucial link in the chain of transmission before the final designation of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri. The text reflects the scholarly tradition of validating the Imam's representatives through personal testimony from the Imam's own family, reinforcing the legitimacy of the Ghaybah period's leadership structure.
